Vernicha James became our first global champion since John Regis when she won the World Junior 200 metre Championship in Jamaica. Incredibly, Amy Spencer, at 16 years of age, was also in the final of that race and both won silver and bronze medals in the GB relay squads.
and not to mention Belgrave club record holder over 100, 200 and 400 metres, Vernicha James still has another season in the Under 20 age group.

Vernicha James set senior club records at 100m, 200m and 400m in 2002. She represented Britain in the Spar European Cup Superleague, won the Commonwealth Games 200m trial and ran in the bronze medal winning 4x100m team in Manchester.

Unfortunately, the previous winner of the women's 200 metre title, our own Vernicha James, was unable to take her place in the line-up for the 2003 championship, having been unable to rid herself of the hamstring injury that has been dogging her since the indoor season.

Vernicha James was also selected but had to withdraw due to injury. In the World Student Games, we were represented by Chris Lambert (won gold in the 100 m), Matt Douglas (won silver in the 400m hurdles and bronze in the 4x400 m relay), Goldie Sayers and Michelle Carey.
